_what: The caps Trillion holds, each with where it is enforced and why it exists, so a refusal can say what the cap is and why (src/limits.mjs limitSaid) and an audit can find a cap nobody explained (unregisteredLimits). The number itself stays in its owner's DATA file (`owner` file, `path` inside it): this file never repeats a value, it explains one. A row is { id (owner file name without .json, a dot, the key), owner (repo path of the DATA file), path (keys from the file's root to the number), what (the thing being capped, as a noun phrase that starts a sentence), bound (`most` or `least`), unit (plural noun), source (the code that enforces it), why (what the cap protects, one sentence) }. A new cap is one row here; test/limits.test.mjs fails if a row points at a number that is not there.

words.unknown: {id} is not a cap Trillion explains.

rows.why: A shorter pursuit carries too little meaning to match any move against.
It is read as one pursuit and embedded once; a longer text is several pursuits at once and stops matching any one.
The job becomes the instructions of one handoff an AI reads in a single go.

rows.what: The line the person may see about a job
rows.why: It is the line the person may see about the job, so it stays a sentence.
The id is the key that makes one handoff per account and job, so it stays short enough to key on.

rows.what: The jobs Trillion keeps for people's AIs
rows.why: Every connecting AI has the jobs that hold for it checked against its account, so the whole set stays bounded; end one to add another.
